entry.title: Assos Beach, Behramkale
entry.summary: Assos is a stone village on a hill above the northern Aegean, with the ruins of a Temple of Athena at the top and a small harbour below. The pebble coast at the foot of the village is quiet and quaint, and it makes a calm stop on the north Aegean route.

entry.title: Marmaris Beach, Mugla
entry.summary: Marmaris Beach lies along the sheltered bay at Marmaris, with a long seafront of sand and pebbles. The town, marina and castle are close by, and boats run from here to coves and beaches around the bay.

entry.title: Side Beach, Manavgat
entry.summary: Side has long beaches of fine sand on both sides of a small peninsula holding the ancient town and the Temple of Apollo. The water is shallow and gentle, and the old streets, shops and ruins are a short walk from the sand.

entry.title: Beldibi Beach, Kemer
entry.summary: Beldibi is a pebble beach between Antalya and Kemer, with the Taurus Mountains rising steeply behind the coast. The sea is clear, and the shore has fewer crowds than the central resort beaches.

entry.title: Dikili Beach, Izmir
entry.summary: Dikili is a small Aegean town north of Izmir, with a beach that looks across the water toward the Greek island of Lesbos. It is mostly visited by Turkish holidaymakers, so the atmosphere is local and calm.

entry.title: Datca Beach, Mugla
entry.summary: Datca is a laid-back town at the western end of a long peninsula between the Aegean and the Mediterranean. The town beach has clear water and is backed by cafes and small shops, and the pace is slower than in nearby Marmaris or Bodrum.

entry.title: Adrasan Beach, Kumluca
entry.summary: Adrasan is a calm bay in a green valley on the Lycian coast, with a pebble beach and a few small pensions and restaurants. Boat trips run from the bay to Suluada island, and the village feels far quieter than the large resorts near Antalya.

entry.title: Badavut Beach, Ayvalik
entry.summary: Badavut is a sandy beach on the Aegean coast near Ayvalik, in the north of the Turkish Aegean. The setting is calmer than the big southern resorts, with olive groves inland and a relaxed local atmosphere.

entry.title: Altinkum Beach, Didim
entry.summary: Altinkum is a wide, golden sandy beach in Didim on the Aegean coast, with very shallow water that suits young children. Its name means golden sand in Turkish, and the town behind the beach has hotels, cafes and shops.

entry.title: Gumusluk Beach, Bodrum
entry.summary: Gumusluk is a quiet fishing village on the west of the Bodrum peninsula, with a small sandy beach and a bay sheltered by an islet. Seafood restaurants sit directly on the water, and the setting is a calm alternative to the busier resort towns.

entry.title: Akyaka Beach, Mugla
entry.summary: Akyaka is a village at the head of Gokova Bay, known for traditional wooden houses and a cold river that meets the sea. The beach is calm and sheltered, and the area suits a quiet, low-key stay.

entry.title: Calis Beach, Fethiye
entry.summary: Calis Beach is a long stretch of coarse sand and pebbles beside Fethiye with a seafront promenade. It is known for sunset views over the bay, and cafes and restaurants line the road behind the beach.

entry.title: Kemer Beach, Antalya
entry.summary: Kemer Beach is a long pebble beach beside the resort town of Kemer, with the Taurus Mountains rising behind the coast. The sea is clear, and the seafront has cafes, shops and a marina close by.

entry.title: Ilica Beach, Cesme
entry.summary: Ilica is a sandy beach on the Cesme peninsula with very shallow water, and its name refers to the thermal springs found in this area. It is a popular family beach with cafes and a lively summer atmosphere.

entry.title: Turunc Beach, Marmaris
entry.summary: Turunc is a small village on a green bay south-west of Marmaris, with a pebble and sand beach and hills rising behind the seafront. The water is clear and the atmosphere is quieter than in Marmaris itself.

entry.title: Bitez Beach, Bodrum
entry.summary: Bitez is a long, calm bay on the Bodrum peninsula with a gently shelving seabed and a seafront of cafes and small hotels. It is quieter than central Bodrum and is popular with families and windsurfers.

entry.title: Phaselis Bay, Kemer
entry.summary: Phaselis is a ruined ancient harbour city on a pine-covered peninsula near Kemer, with three small bays beside the ruins. The water is clear and sheltered, and the shore is a mix of pebbles and sand. Swimming among ancient stones makes it feel different from the resort beaches nearby.

entry.title: Alacati Beach, Cesme
entry.summary: Alacati is a shallow bay on the Aegean coast near Cesme, known for steady winds and one of the best windsurfing and kitesurfing scenes in Turkey. The stone houses of Alacati town are a short drive away, and the bay has beach clubs and schools along the water.

entry.title: Icmeler Beach, Marmaris
entry.summary: Icmeler is a sandy bay beach in a resort village a short distance from Marmaris. The water is calm and shallow, and cafes, shops and restaurants line the seafront. It suits families who want a gentle swim and services close to the sand.

entry.title: Konyaalti Beach, Antalya
entry.summary: Konyaalti is a long pebble beach on the western side of Antalya, with the Taurus Mountains rising behind the sea. A promenade runs along the shore, and the city, shops and restaurants are close by. The sea is clear and the beach is easy to reach.

entry.title: Kabak Bay, Fethiye
entry.summary: Kabak is a quiet bay at the bottom of a forested valley near Faralya, on the Lycian Way walking route. The beach is reached by a steep road and paths, and small camps and cafes serve the few visitors. It feels far from the resort coast.

entry.title: Cleopatra Beach, Alanya
entry.summary: Cleopatra Beach is a long stretch of fine golden sand on the west side of the castle hill in Alanya. Legend says Cleopatra and Mark Antony swam here, which gave the beach its name. The sea is shallow and calm, and the town is a short walk away.

entry.title: Butterfly Valley Beach, Faralya
entry.summary: Butterfly Valley is a hidden cove at the foot of steep cliffs and a forested canyon near Faralya. Most visitors arrive by boat from Oludeniz, and there is no road to the beach. The setting is quiet and dramatic, with a small waterfall inside the valley.

entry.title: Iztuzu Beach, Dalyan
entry.summary: Iztuzu is a long, narrow sandy beach on a sandbar between the Mediterranean and the Dalyan river delta. It is a protected nesting site for loggerhead turtles, so rules apply to keep the sand and the night-time beach undisturbed. Boats run to the beach from Dalyan.

entry.title: Cirali Beach, Kemer
entry.summary: Cirali is a long pebble beach in a small protected village near the ancient city of Olympos. Pensions and simple restaurants sit behind the beach instead of large hotels, and the Chimaera flames burn on the hillside a short walk away. Sea turtles nest on this coast.

entry.title: Patara Beach, Kas
entry.summary: Patara is one of the longest sandy beaches on the Turkish coast, with dunes behind it and the ruins of the ancient Lycian city of Patara close by. The sea is clear with waves at times, and the beach feels open and uncrowded outside peak season. Sea turtles nest here, so keep to marked areas.

entry.title: Kaputas Beach, Kalkan
entry.summary: Kaputas is a small sandy cove at the mouth of a narrow canyon on the coast road between Kalkan and Kas. It is reached by a long flight of steps down from the road, and the water is a vivid turquoise.

entry.title: Oludeniz Beach, Fethiye
entry.summary: Oludeniz is a famous turquoise lagoon and beach near Fethiye, backed by pine-covered mountains. The sheltered lagoon has calm, clear water, and the main beach is a mix of sand and pebbles. Paragliders from Babadag mountain land on the seafront, which adds to the scene.

entry.title: Pomos Beach, Tillyria
entry.summary: Pomos is a small fishing village on the Tillyria coast with a pebble shoreline and a quiet atmosphere. It is a calm place to swim and eat fish away from the busier resorts.

entry.title: Kato Pyrgos Beach, Tillyria
entry.summary: Kato Pyrgos is a remote pebble coast in the Tillyria region, far from the big resorts. The beaches are quiet, the scenery is wild, and a few simple tavernas serve the area.
